feedback.problem:
What is the smallest possible distance between the points $(-4x,\,2x-3)$ and $(1,\,5),$ where $x$ is a real number? Do not round the answer.

The smallest possible distance is
{{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's compute the *squared* distance $S(x)$ between the two points. We have

$$
\begin{aligned}S(x) & ={((-4x)-1)}^{2}+{((2x-3)-5)}^{2} \\  & =(-4x-1)^{2}+(2x-8)^{2} \\  & =16{x}^{2}+8x+1+4{x}^{2}-32x+64 \\  & =20{x}^{2}-24x+65.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we want to minimize $S,$ we compute the derivative ${S}^{′}(x).$ This gives

$$
{S}^{′}(x)=40x-24.
$$

The stationary points of $S(x)$ are the points where the derivative ${S}^{′}(x)=0.$ Solving this equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}^{′}(x) & =0 \\ 40x-24 & =0 \\ x & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can see that ${S}^{″}(\frac{3}{5})=40>0.$

So, the squared distance (and therefore the actual distance) reaches a minimum when $x=\frac{3}{5}.$ 

Since $S(x)$ gives the squared distance between the two points, the actual distance $d$ between the two points when $x=\frac{3}{5}$ is given by

$$
d=\sqrt{S(\frac{3}{5})}.
$$

Computing this quantity, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =\sqrt{S(\frac{3}{5})} \\  & =\sqrt{20{(\frac{3}{5})}^{2}-24(\frac{3}{5})+65} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{289}{5}} \\  & =\frac{17}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{17\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the smallest possible distance between the points $(-4x,\,2x-3)$ and $(1,\,5)$ is $\frac{17\sqrt{5}}{5}.$
